title: Arbitrary small set colimits as quotients of disjoint unions
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small category, possibly empty, and $F:I\to\mathbf{Set}_{\mathcal U}$ a functor. Use colimits in the universal-property sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. On the disjoint union $S=\coprod_{i\in\operatorname{Ob}I}F(i)$ define $R((i,x),(j,y))$ to mean that there is an arrow $a:i\to j$ with $F(a)(x)=y$, and let $\sim$ be the smallest equivalence relation containing $R$. Then $Q=S/{\sim}$ is a $\mathcal U$-small set, and the maps $\iota_i:F(i)\to Q$, $x\mapsto[i,x]$, form a colimit cocone. Every element of $Q$ has a representative $[i,x]$, and $[i,x]=[j,y]$ if and only if $(i,x)\sim(j,y)$. Thus maps out of $Q$ are exactly families of maps out of the $F(i)$ agreeing along all arrows of $I$. For empty $I$, $Q=\varnothing$.
